title: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Second Reading vote requirement
sections.summary: A vote is taken to confirm the Second Reading is supported by at least two-thirds of Elected and Non-Constituency Members, which is 61 Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: If not, the Question is, "That the Bill be now read a Second time." Pursuant to Article 5(2) of the Constitution, a vote is taken to ascertain that the Second Reading of the Bill is supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament, which is 61 Members.

sections.label: Second Reading carried, Third Reading vote
sections.summary: With 72 Ayes and no Noes or Abstentions, the Second Reading is carried, and a vote is taken on the Third Reading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Second Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-constituency Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That the Bill be now read a Third time." Pursuant to Article 5(2) of the Constitution, a vote is taken to ascertain that the Third Reading of the Bill is supported by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament, which is 61 Members.

sections.label: Third Reading carried
sections.summary: With 72 Ayes and no Noes or Abstentions, the Third Reading is carried by at least two-thirds of Elected and Non-Constituency Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Third Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-constituency Members of Parliament.
